item.text: Run a four-week “staff discovery” experiment in one clearly marked section of the bookstore, using a small number of shelf labels rather than rearranging the entire store. Select twelve unfamiliar or underrepresented authors across several genres, and place one or two copies of each near popular, related titles, with simple cards saying “If you like this, try…” and a brief, specific reason to explore the author. Keep the main alphabetical or genre-based organization intact, so regular customers can still navigate easily. Track the featured books’ weekly sales, browsing time, and customer questions, comparing results with similar nonfeatured titles in the same genres. Add a short QR-code survey asking whether shoppers discovered an author, whether the sign was helpful, and whether they found the placement confusing. Ask staff to record informal comments and note which recommendations generate conversation or repeat visits. After four weeks, compare sales and feedback with the previous four-week period, while accounting for promotions and seasonal changes. If discovery increases without complaints about navigation, retain the most effective signs and expand the test gradually to another section. If results are weak, revise the wording, pairings, or author selection before investing in a broader redesign.
